feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid technical breadth. It is well written overall, but it is slightly repetitive, a bit dense in places, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcomes and tightening structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director-level leadership; this strengthens credibility and signals promotion based on performance.  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, skills, and experience; the CV consistently supports the “Digital Communications & Strategy Lead” positioning.  
- Good use of scale indicators and platforms (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million page views, GA4, Drupal, BigQuery), which adds substance and technical credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, reduced publishing time, campaign performance, or team/budget size. This would improve impact.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); and replace markdown formatting in Languages (**English**) with plain text.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of seniority, sector focus, or platform scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add a clearer positioning line tied to recent roles, e.g., public-sector/member association digital leadership, Drupal modernization, and enterprise content operations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with tighter, higher-impact wording such as “multi-channel digital communications and platform strategy.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in Drupal modernization, editorial workflows, analytics, and cross-functional governance, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is supported by experience, but avoid overemphasizing it if targeting broader digital strategy roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and standardize wording: “Multi-channel communications” instead of “communication.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership strengths over generic execution tasks; e.g., lead with digital strategy, governance, editorial systems, analytics, and platform modernization.
- Consider a tighter version: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform & CMS management • Multi-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow & systems design • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- If space allows elsewhere, replace “Web & CMS administration” with “Web platform management” for a more senior tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, multi-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented position. Tighten the phrasing, foreground ownership, and connect the work to visible outcomes or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: led, built, redesigned, implemented, established, launched.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and add outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, workflow time reduced, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search/discovery improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, creating modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing toolkits; improved publishing flexibility and cross-team campaign execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the NACo Director role; keep this item focused on what is new: consulting scope, Drupal builds, AI search, and enterprise web improvement.
- AI-enabled search also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same description verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest metrics: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements in publishing speed, reporting adoption, engagement, production cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance from the in-house studio.
- Tighten channel language: replace “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands…” with a more outcome-driven line such as audience growth, engagement lift, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate earlier NACo bullets unless framed here as studio buildout and scaled production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid mid-level progression item, but it reads as a softer precursor to the stronger Director role. Tighten it around execution, channel ownership, and cross-team coordination, and add any concrete volume/growth metrics to increase impact.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Strengthen the video bullet: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one outcome-focused line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.” Add metrics if available (open rates, production cadence, turnaround time, stakeholder teams supported).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role; emphasize execution and process-building here.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: “enterprise web modernization” or “AI-enabled content discovery” would better reflect current work than generic “content leadership.”
- Keep all items noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership, planning, and messaging styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also echoes the header and multiple NACo roles; use only if this positioning is essential.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-signal or dated items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Enterprise web platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to reduce listiness.
- If space allows, align to recent impact: prioritize Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and automation over older/general tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; avoid repeating the exact phrase verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and decision-making, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting” before listing platforms.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with a broader, senior phrasing like “search, content and conversion performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and measurement frameworks - KPI design and executive reporting - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - Search, content and user-performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid overlisting tools here since the NACo role already provides the strongest proof of analytics platform depth.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value delivery capabilities rather than tool-level items already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task/tool list to outcome-oriented capabilities:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- In-house studio and control-room operations

- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the NACo studio build and leadership scope.

- “PTZ camera systems” is very tool-specific and may be better left to Technical + IT or removed.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, while trimming lower-value items.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show level, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more specific to recent impact: **Drupal 9/10** rather than just Drupal.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- **GitHub Pages** may feel lightweight versus the rest; cut it if you need space for stronger Drupal/SharePoint detail.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless the CV uses versioning consistently; they add little value at this level.
- If accurate, add one impact-oriented qualifier in parentheses, e.g. **API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)** to make the list less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations” in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the broader summary there and making this section more tool-specific.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also fit under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** if you want cleaner categorization.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Power Automate, Zapier | **Workflow/PM:** Airtable, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 lower-value names with outcome-oriented phrasing elsewhere in experience bullets, e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; current title is slightly misleading.
- Repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep this section concise and tool-focused only.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since your recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, this item should signal scale, platform ownership, and audience engagement relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** for clearer alignment with your experience.
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: **Higher Logic (newsletter operations, audience segmentation) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration, CRM-linked campaigns) • Mailchimp (campaign deployment)**
- If space allows, tie to outcomes rather than tools alone: e.g., **Platforms supporting newsletters to tens of thousands of public-sector stakeholders**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email/channel references in multiple NACo roles; keep this item platform-specific and avoid restating newsletter scale elsewhere in the skills section.
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless supported by functions like segmentation, automation, or journey building.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production scope, and team-building contributions without repeating leadership claims covered in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support multi-channel operations across web, email, social, and video.”
- Add sharper outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/audience for weekly videos, or workflow improvements (e.g., faster publishing, more consistent output).
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstractions like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specifics on what you produced or improved.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and video operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and recurring weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows while guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate by framing this as the earlier build/production phase.
- Avoid broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the multimedia work more concise and specific: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications.”
- Elevate the strongest achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language if later NACo roles already cover web/video/social in more depth; keep this entry focused on research support + podcast launch.
- Don’t overstate leadership here, since stronger team/platform leadership appears in 2018–2024 roles.
